description: A small design change has knock-on effects across materials, labor sequencing, and downstream subcontractors, and the team needs a clear map of what else must shift because of it.

user_profile.persona: 39-year-old construction PM managing a live site with frequent small adjustments
user_profile.context: The change seems modest on paper, but experience suggests it could ripple through several later activities
user_profile.communication_style: Impact-oriented and cross-functional, wants secondary effects captured before they surprise the schedule

fact_sheet.fact: Architectural Change Order (ACO-11B) was approved on October 26, 2023, for the Apex Tower project.
ACO-11B modifies the 12th floor layout to reroute a 24-inch HVAC duct to accommodate a new server room chase requested by the client, Innovate Corp.
Alex Chen is the Project Manager for Keystone Construction responsible for implementing ACO-11B; his mobile number is 555-821-4409.
The new HVAC duct path requires a new 26-inch by 14-inch penetration through non-load-bearing steel beam S-12-4B.
SteelFrame Erectors is the subcontractor responsible for cutting the new beam penetration; their site foreman is Marco Diaz.
The change order for SteelFrame Erectors (SCO-SF-05) to perform the beam penetration is priced at $3,850.
The rerouted HVAC duct now directly conflicts with the planned path for electrical conduits EC-12-101 through EC-12-104.
Sarah Jenkins of Voltric Electricals is the project lead managing the electrical rework; her email is s.jenkins@voltric.com.
The revised electrical plan (Drawing E-5.12 Rev 2) requires an additional 80 feet of 2-inch EMT conduit and four new junction boxes.
The new duct location reduces clearance for the main plumbing vent stack P-V-3 to 1.5 inches, which is below the 3-inch building code minimum.
HydroFlow Plumbing must offset the vent stack, requiring two additional 45-degree 4-inch PVC fittings (Part #PVC4-45B).
The original straight HVAC duct section (Part #HV-D24-S10) is now obsolete for this location and must be returned to the supplier, AeroDuct Fabricators.
A new custom-fabricated 24-inch, 90-degree HVAC elbow (Part #HV-D24-E90-C) has been ordered with a 7-business-day lead time.
The new custom HVAC elbow costs $1,200, an increase of $750 over the original straight section.
The additional materials for the electrical reroute (conduit and J-boxes) cost $415 from City Electric Supply.
Drywall framing on the 12th floor, originally scheduled for November 1, 2023, is now on hold until November 10, 2023.
The critical path for the 12th-floor interior fit-out now runs through the delivery and installation of the custom HVAC elbow.
The work sequence requires SteelFrame Erectors to complete the beam cut before HydroFlow Plumbing can begin offsetting the vent stack.
The MEP rough-in inspection for the 12th-floor core with City Inspector Bob Vance (Badge #784) has been moved from October 31 to November 9, 2023.
A coordination meeting for ACO-11B was held on October 27, 2023, at 10:00 AM in the site trailer.
All documents, costs, and schedule changes for ACO-11B are being tracked in Procore under Change Event #045.
The project's BIM model (Apex_Tower_R23.rvt) was updated with the new MEP routes by VDC coordinator Maria Garcia on October 28, 2023.
The dedicated Slack channel for urgent field coordination on this change is #12th-floor-hvac-rework.
The total approved direct cost impact of ACO-11B, including all subcontractor change orders and material upcharges, is $7,920.
The cost of the change order will be drawn from the project's design contingency fund, which has a remaining balance of $152,400.
Elena Vargas of Skyline Architects is the architect of record who provided the sign-off for the new beam penetration.
Keystone Construction's on-site superintendent, Frank Miller, is responsible for updating the daily log with all rework activities.
Job Hazard Analysis form #JHA-SF-115 was created for the overhead steel cutting, requiring a 20-foot exclusion zone and a dedicated fire watch.
